**Observation Log:**

[SESSION DATE] Session Date: 2023/03/15 (Wed) 10:44  
[EVENT] User just got a smoker today.  
[PREFERENCE] User is excited to experiment with different types of wood and meats.  
[PREFERENCE] User is considering trying a mix of hickory and apple wood.  
[PREFERENCE] User has heard that hickory and apple wood pair well with pork and beef.  
[ASSISTANT] Recommended meat and wood pairings:  
[ASSISTANT] Pork: Hickory and Apple Wood, Cherry Wood, Pecan Wood.  
[ASSISTANT] Beef: Post Oak Wood, Mesquite Wood, Oak Wood.  
[ASSISTANT] Chicken and Sausages: Apple Wood, Cherry Wood, Maple Wood.  
[ASSISTANT] Lamb and Game Meats: Oak Wood, Hickory Wood, Pecan Wood.  
[PREFERENCE] User has heard that wood chips or chunks can be used instead of logs.  
[ASSISTANT] Explained the difference between wood chips and chunks.  
[ASSISTANT] Wood Chips: Small, ignite quickly, good for quick bursts of smoke.  
[ASSISTANT] Wood Chunks: Larger, burn slower, good for longer smoke times.  
[ASSISTANT] Recommended soaking wood chips or chunks in water for at least 30 minutes before use.  
[PREFERENCE] User has heard that wood pellets can be used as an alternative to logs, chips, or chunks.  
[ASSISTANT] Explained what wood pellets are and their advantages.  
[ASSISTANT] Wood pellets are small, compressed pellets made from dried and processed wood fibers.  
[ASSISTANT] Advantages of wood pellets: convenience, consistency, efficiency, space-saving, cost-effective.  
[ASSISTANT] Recommended brands of wood pellets: Lumberjack Pellets, Traeger Pellets, BBQr's Delight Pellets, Pit Barrel Pellets, Cookin' Pellets.  
[ASSISTANT] Recommended types of wood pellets: Hickory Pellets, Apple Pellets, Cherry Pellets, Oak Pellets, Mesquite Pellets.  
[PREFERENCE] User is considering trying out wood pellets for their smoker.  
[PREFERENCE] User has heard that wood pellets are more efficient and produce a consistent smoke flavor.
